In addition to doing standalone runs and bike rides, I recommend practicing biking then running a few times leading up to the race. It doesn't need to be a big run or bike, even 10 minutes of running is fine. These workouts are called "bricks" because your legs tend to feel like bricks when you start running after biking.

I also recommend practicing your "transitions." This is where you switch from run to bike and back to run again. In the race, you will have a designated spot where you rack your bike (while running) and can leave other items like running shoes, visor, water bottle, etc. With lots of people around you, it can be a bit disorienting doing transitions the first time, so it's good to practice (e.g., practice setting your bike in its place, then removing your helmet, then putting your hat on, etc.).

I use my food scale all the time!

First, a food scale is way more accurate than using cups or estimating serving sizes. But, there are even more benefits.

One is that a food scale saves you from dirtying extra dishes. For example, instead of measuring out 1 cup of cereal into a measuring cup and then pouring that cereal into a bowl, I just set my bowl on the scale and then pour in cereal until the scale reads 30 grams or whatever the weight of a cup of that cereal is, according to the packaging.

Second, scales are great when baking. In many parts of the world, recipes are commonly written with ingredients by weight instead of volume because it's much more accurate. (Tell two people to scoop out "1 cup" of flour using a measuring cup and they will have totally different amounts because of how flour can settle in a cup). Writing a recipe to call for, say, 200 grams of flour is way more precise. And, again, you save on dishes because you can pour ingredients directly into your mixing bowl.

So, I'd say don't worry about your family. Get a scale!

**INGREDIENTS**

- 1/2 cup creamy peanut butter (regular or reduced fat)

- 1/3 cup honey

- 1 large egg

- 2 Tablespoons canola oil

- 1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla extract

- 3 1/2 cups old-fashioned oats

- 1/2 cup packed light brown sugar

- 1/2 teaspoon salt

- 1/3 cup peanut butter chips

- 1/3 cup mini chocolate chips

**INSTRUCTIONS**

Preheat the oven to 350°F and line a 13x9-inch nonstick baking pan with cooking spray.

In a large bowl, beat the peanut butter, honey, egg, oil, and vanilla extract with a handheld beater until smooth and creamy.

In a separate medium bowl, stir together the oats, brown sugar, and salt. Add the oat mixture to the peanut butter mixture and stir until well combined, then stir in the peanut butter chips and mini chocolate chips.

Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking pan, pressing it into an even layer.

Bake for 12 to 15 minutes or until the edges are golden brown. Remove the pan from the oven and let it cool completely before slicing the granola into bars and serving.
